messages:
andrea: Heads-up: CPU regression on master after the kernel-selector change. small-input p50 +18%. did a quick perf run, attaching notes.

sam: oh — which change? the dynamic kernel picker?

andrea: yep. commit 9f4b2c. i think we're spending more time in python callbacks that stash kernel metadata.

maya: can repro locally. started `perf record` on the worker with the tiny input set. `perf report` shows lots of time in PyObject_Call and our batch_manager marshal path.

andrea: saw a pattern of many short, repeated frames in the folded stacks — stackwalk shows thin frames over and over.

perf-bot: Perf job queued: https://ci.redwood/prof/1718102030-1 (nsys/perf artifacts uploaded)

jordan: can you paste the `perf top` samples you saw?

maya: ```
 22.4%  python           PyObject_Call
 14.8%  python           batch_manager::marshal_request
  9.2%  libc-2.31        memcpy
  7.1%  python           _PyEval_EvalFrameDefault
```

andrea: memcpy spikes line up with small buffer copies in the tokenizer path. i suspect the batcher is copying small slices per request.

sam: right now the batcher calls a per-request callback to build tensors. the kernel-descriptor struct got converted into an ephemeral dict recently, so we may be allocating a lot.

maya: i ran `perf record -g --call-graph dwarf` and also `py-spy` to capture python stacks. `py-spy` shows many brief stacks in `prepare_request` and the callback wrapper.

andrea: proposal: pre-allocate a per-worker scratch buffer and write into that, avoid small mallocs/copies. also consider lazy construction of kernel metadata after KV-cache lookup.

jordan: can we gate this with a feature flag so we can roll it quickly? quick experiment: avoid copying the kernel descriptor until after KV cache hits.

sam: SG. i'll prototype: in `batch_manager.py` pass a lightweight pointer/tuple instead of a full dict in the hot loop.

maya: before merging, let's rerun perf + stack-collapse to check the folded stacks. please run with `perf record -g --call-graph dwarf` to get accurate C/Python transitions.

andrea: also add a micro p50 regression check for the small input set in CI so we catch this next time.

perf-bot: Perf artifacts available: https://ci.redwood/prof/1718102030-1/trace.gz

jordan: if someone can add a minimal reproducer in a docker image i can run the flamegraph pipeline and instrument the memcpy hotspots.

sam: on it — i'll push a small PR with the prototype and perf numbers attached.

maya: thanks — i'll validate with py-spy + perf and post before/after stacks.

andrea: :thumbsup:
